newsitem.title: USA: Key Democrat to vote against budget accord -aide.
newsitem.headline: Key Democrat to vote against budget accord -aide.

text.p: House Minority Leader Richard Gephardt will vote against the balanced budget worked out with the White House and will inform fellow Democrats of his decision at a meeting Tuesday, a top Democratic aide said.

"At the (Democratic) caucus he is going to say he is going to vote against it and why," the aide said. He noted the decision is consistent with Gephardt's statements around the country in the past two years that he would not vote to cut Medicare to fund tax cuts which benefit the wealthy.

Democrats felt they were hurt at the polls in 1994 after their votes in the first year of Clinton's term to raise taxes. Gephardt is the leading contender to challenge Vice President Al Gore for the party's 2000 presidential nomination.

The Democratic aide said Gephardt would argue that the budget agreement does not bring the deficit to zero by 2000 as claimed. "It is not a balanced budget and it is not going to be fair to the public so there is little reason to vote for it," he said.

Gephardt and liberal Democrats have been expected to oppose the budget when it comes before the full House late Tuesday. But budget leaders have said they expect the broad middle of both parties to unite for its passage. The budget deal has come under attack from Republican conservatives who would like to see deeper cuts in government spending and larger tax cuts.

The Senate is also expected to pass it this week. The five-year balanced budget plan was worked out during months of negotiations between the White House and Republican congressional leaders. In addition to reducing the deficit, it calls for a net $85 billion tax cut over the next five years.
